But that's not all - plants also use sunlight to regulate their growth and development. The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis produce ATP and NADPH, which are used to power the light-independent reactions, also known as the Calvin cycle. This cycle fixes carbon dioxide into glucose, providing the plant with the energy it needs to grow and thrive.

In addition to photosynthesis, plants also use sunlight to regulate their circadian rhythms, which are the internal biological clocks that control the plant's daily activities. The light-dark cycle helps plants to synchronize their growth and development with the changing seasons, ensuring that they are prepared for the challenges of each time of year.

As I watched the sunlight dance through the leaves of my grandmother's plants, I realized that it was more than just a source of energy - it was a vital component of their very existence.
